title: What is mountaintop removal mining?
summary: Josh and Chuck explain mountaintop removal mining, a strip-mining method in which coal companies blast off the tops of mountains to reach horizontal coal seams. They cover the process (clear cutting, explosives, draglines, overburden dumped into valley fills), burial of streams, coal slurry and earthen impoundment dam failures (Buffalo Creek, West Virginia, 1972; Kentucky, 2000), selenium-contaminated waters and deformed fish, fly rock deaths, health problems in Appalachian communities (including March Fork Elementary School), economic arguments versus costs, the Powell River Project reclamation example, and regulatory fights involving the EPA, Obama administration, and a Senate bill from Mitch McConnell and Rand Paul. The episode closes with an interview and song by musician and activist Ben Sollee, who discusses his album Inclusions-era work, the Deer Companion album, and I Love Mountains. Note: the transcript is an auto-generated, error-prone text; names and figures are reproduced as they appear in the hosts' speech where settled.

segments.title: Opening banter and West Virginia mining job losses
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, then Josh sets up the episode with the statistic that West Virginia's employed miners fell from sixty thousand to twenty-two thousand since 1979 even as coal output rose, and introduces mountaintop removal mining and the upcoming interview with Ben Sollee.

segments.title: How mountaintop removal works
segments.summary: The hosts contrast traditional underground mining with mountaintop removal, describing clear cutting, blasting off up to hundreds of feet of mountain, the use of draglines and large shovels, and the resulting barren 'moonscape.'

segments.title: Valley fills and buried streams
segments.summary: Overburden is dumped into nearby valleys, a practice called valley fill, which has buried more than twelve miles of headwaters and streams. Permits, cost comparisons between trucking and pushing material, and the number of valley fill permits are discussed.

segments.title: Coal slurry and dam failures
segments.summary: Coal washing produces toxic coal slurry stored in impoundments behind earthen dams. The hosts describe the 1972 Buffalo Creek dam collapse in West Virginia and a 2000 Kentucky slurry spill into the Tug Fork of the Big Sandy River, and the company head's act of God comment.

segments.title: Reclamation and the Powell River Project
segments.summary: The hosts discuss reclamation requirements under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act, the limits of reclamation in practice, and the Powell River Project in Virginia as a rare example of a restored site now used as a wildlife preserve.
topics: Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act

segments.title: Environmental impacts: selenium, fish, drinking water, streams
segments.summary: A Science study found deformed fish with toxic selenium levels in most sampled streams. Drinking water risks from leaking dams are mentioned, and the Army Corps of Engineers reportedly could not point to a successful stream creation project.

segments.title: Human health, explosives and fly rock deaths
segments.summary: Explosive use by the coal industry, noise, and fly rock are covered, including a 2004 death of a three-year-old boy in his bed from a boulder, and deaths from floods, mudslides and overloaded coal trucks. A public health study estimated hundreds of deaths per year in Appalachia tied to coal mining.

segments.title: March Fork Elementary and Massey Energy risks
segments.summary: The hosts describe the risk of a three-billion-gallon coal slurry pond above March Fork Elementary School, illnesses reported by parents, a documentary about a rally at the West Virginia governor's office, and Massey Energy's role, including a former executive appointed to a Department of Energy post.

segments.title: Economics, energy share and policy debate
segments.summary: The hosts compare coal's eight-billion-dollar economic contribution with a forty-two-billion-dollar estimated health and life cost, note that mountaintop removal supplies a small share of U.S. coal energy, and discuss EPA leadership, Clean Water Act rule changes, and the Obama administration's stricter guidelines. The McConnell and Paul bill to restrict the EPA is described.

segments.title: Further reading and show plugs
segments.summary: The hosts recommend resources on the topic, including Jonathan Franzen's novel Freedom, the TV show Justified, a documentary about the Whites of West Virginia, and the groups I Love Mountains, Mountain Justice Summer, and Appalachian Voices.

segments.title: Interview with Ben Sollee
segments.summary: Musician and cellist Ben Sollee discusses his album Deer Companion, produced with Jim James and Daniel Martin Moore and released on Subpop, with proceeds going to Appalachian Voices. He describes his activism, bicycle touring, and the connection between Appalachian heritage and electricity use. The episode closes with his song Electrified and a sign-off plugging his tour.
